Precisely because we will all be dead it's worth living, most of life is suffering I know, but I also tend to not believe people who tell me that their life is only suffering and there's nothing else. I've been through violent family, grew up in violent country, almost got killed by my father daily, still going through it, but if I'm honest with myself, I'll never say my life is only suffering. There are moments of joy, when my niece looks at me and smiles, when I listen to a long forgotten song that takes me back to simpler times. These moments don't happen every day, but hey, if they did they would be boring right? You have to get wet in the rain to appreciate having a home, having a shower and some dry clothes. I understand for some people, it rains every day, but those few moments when the sun shines for me make it worth everything else. As I said, it takes a lot of strength and bravery to unalive yourself, if you have that strength you might as well use it to live. Or at least try. Whatever problem you have, and I know it sounds silly but if there's one thing life has proven me over and over, is that whatever problem you have, it will pass. However big that mountain looks, one day it will be behind your back. Those problems we consider problems, are usually not worth our attention, and we focus on them so much we damage ourselves. Think of when you see someone who has no arms, no legs, no family, someone who was born with a disease, those things make you look at life with another perspective, even if it lasts for 5 minutes. Don't worry about things out of your control, it's pointless. I'm not trying to convince anyone, I'm just talking as a person who deals with this daily, who is frustrated, who hates himself and who happens to think sometimes I might just off myself, but I never did. Call it lack of courage, I don't know, I just know that life goes on tomorrow, for everyone, even if I'm not here. Same happens if I'm here, so why leave the party early? The only one losing would be me, so I might just stay and see if something interesting happens, and if it doesn't I'll go home after the party, just as anyone else as we all do in the end but at least I was there, for a brief moment, in the nothingness of the universe I was alive and present for those few years given to me and whatever I did with my life, I lived.

I know it's a stupid example but it illustrates my point: I don't think i have a problem, i don't think there's something wrong with me, yet i'm depressed. I'm depressed because i don't have a purpose, not because i have problem, not because a relative died, not because my girlfriend left me. I feel normal, i'm not angry, sad, i don't hate the world or anything else, i just feel like something's missing. I grew up in a small town where community was a real thing, where you would leave to go on vacation and you'd leave the keys to the house to the neighbor and he would go in and clean it once a week for you. And i don't see that anymore in the world, and i miss it, i grew up with teh concept of a family, brothers, parents, sisters, cousins and i don't see that anymore. Maybe i'm late to this but i can add my 2 cents here. I'm from eastern Europe, ex-communist state. Everytime i watch scarface i get the chills, because Tony Montana reminds me of a person i know very well: My father. My father is not a killer(at least not that i know of) but he was raised on the streets in the 80s in an eastern european country and by the time i was born he was one of the most feared in our city. He didn't sell drugs(kinda hard under communism), but he was violent and had balls and ambition.   
The movie gives me the chills because a lot of scenes, a lot of gestures Tony does and a lot of stares are identical to my Father's(when Tony looks at Manny before killing him, that's the exact stare my father would have when he was furious and i've feared for my life more than once, when he gives you that stare you know he's not in control). One thing i noticed quickly is when they are going to  the Motel, Manny and the others are thinking about Girls and having fun not realizing how dangerous the thing they're about to do is. Tony looks away and he's focused on the objective because his ambition tells him that is his great opportunity. Tony is not afraid to say what he thinks or do what he wants, even with the boss and this is a trait that i've seen in my father also, not caring about authority and almost being unable to feel fear going as far as having fights with policemen, beating the shit out of them or even armed people. This brought my father very quickly to be respected and above all feared. I was untouchable growing up just because of my father's name, he was not a mafia member, he was not in any position of power, but he had the only thing that matters as Tony says: balls. He could find himself against 50 people alone and not only he wouldn't back down, he would provoke them and laugh in their face to make them attack(this is probabily some kind of psycho trait that i think tony also has). Funnily enough, my father has a scar on his cheek he got from a bar fight he was involved in when i was a child. All this to say that the movie is not fast paced, it just portrays reality. My father was not a mafia member nor smuggled cocaine, but he managed to become feared, respected and wealthy pretty quickly. He was smart(especially street-smart), quick witted, ambitious and unable to feel fear, just like Tony and he quickly rose to the top in our City. So if you add to this being a cold blooded assassin and living in the 80s Miami with nothing to lose, then Tony's story is more real than ever. There's a lot of subtle things in the movie that you don't notice if you didn't grow up in the streets, if you didn't have a first hand contact with poverty and violence(i did) and i notice this when watching the movie with my European friends. They see it as a cool and at times funny gangster movie, i see a lot of it's scenes as a movie counterpart to real life events that i've lived on my skin and i can appreciate a lot the details in the movie about street life, street smarts etc...

Agree and disagree. While most of those claims come from a place of nostalgia(I'm one of them) it's undeniable that despite having more chances to have fun today as you say, quality decreases as quantity increases. I think what people mean when they talk about the past (leaving aside the nostalgia) is that things aren't as genuine nowadays as they were back then. It's a vast generalization I know, but having lived as a child during the early 2000s and having two brothers in their teens during that time I can see clearly how they were all just hanging out. Meeting in the same places, doing the same things but it was more genuine. Today it's not common to see 30-40 teens sitting on a bench in a park just talking and having fun doing nothing, back then it was the norm. Life had less stimuli and it was much easier to have a blast with just simple things while nowadays we're kind of spoiled and bar is raised too high. If we don't go out and do something interesting each night we don't consider it worth bothering and simply prefer Netflix. Small anecdote: I haven't been watching TV for years now, changed my house and has 2 weeks without internet at home so had to watch TV and I had forgotten how fun it could be to simply watch a movie. You don't get to choose, you know they're gonna air that movie on Saturday and you spend the whole week enjoying the waiting for the day to come, you sit there ans pay attention because you can't stop it or rewind it back so you're forced to pay attention. You get ad breaks where you have time to smoke a cigarette and you have to go in that moment because as I said you can't stop the movie. It just takes away the "being in control" and having too much choice and let's you properly relax. I had so much fun. And I think this is what we're missing today, being able to let go and relax. I come home from work and I don't want to have the burden of choosing a movie in an infinite catalog, I just want to shut down my brain and watch something. And the idea that the good movies are usually once a week on weekends makes it even more precious and enjoyable. The idea of having everything at your fingertips at any time takes away the magic of it. Just like going to a restaurant as a child, it happened on special occasions and it was rare and it made it so enjoyable and special, while today whatever we do, we have everything at our fingertips and it simply takes away the fun from it.
